jobs.title: Executive Director of Corporate and Foundation Relations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

In 1965, the University of California, Irvine was founded with a mission to catalyze the community and enhance lives through rigorous academics, cutting-edge research, and dedicated public service. A top public university, UC Irvine is internationally recognized for improving lives through research and discovery, fostering excellence in scholarship and teaching, and engaging and enriching the community. Today, UCI continues to inspire change and pioneer new ideas with the support of its generous partners, alumni and friends.

Through the combined efforts of the University Advancement & Alumni relations team, the University can share its amazing achievements, build lasting relationships, and generate support for important campus programs and initiatives. University Advancement seeks to strengthen contributions to research, education, and service; accelerate the university's place among globally preeminent research universities; and bring together passions, skills, and creativity to further improve people's lives.

Located in Central Development, the Corporate and Foundation Relations team works with administrators, faculty, program directors and development officers to build effective partner relationships, working to understand the needs and priorities of corporations, corporate foundations, associations, and private foundations and to facilitate partnerships to advance UC Irvine's mission.

Your Role on the Team

Under the general direction of the Associate Vice Chancellor, Strategic Philanthropy, and located in University Advancement’s Central unit, the Executive Director of Corporate and Foundation Relations (ED) provides leadership and direction for a comprehensive foundation and corporate relations strategy for UC Irvine. Working closely with academic, administrative and development leaders, the ED will develop proactive strategies to increase philanthropic and corporate support for research, university priorities and interdisciplinary initiatives.

Leads and manages the Corporate and Foundation Relations (CFR) team whose goal is to enhance and strengthen existing University relationships with corporations, corporate foundations, associations like the American Cancer Society, and private foundations, as well as increase funding to the university from these organizations. Develops strategies for identifying and building relationships with new philanthropists and their organizations, helps develop strategies for major gifts and grants with both existing funders and aspirational foundations, and monitors stewardship plans for strategic corporate and foundation donors. In collaboration with the Associate Vice Chancellor for Strategic Philanthropy, may be consulted by the Office of Research about contemplated Organized Research Units (ORUs) and other emerging research initiatives to provide insight on corporate and foundation funding opportunities, sponsor alignment, funding competitiveness, and strategies to enhance external support.

Demonstrated ability to secure seven-figure gifts from foundations, associations and/or corporate foundations and record of proactive outreach to organizations resulting in new relationships and/or funding. Expected to raise an initial annual goal of $4+ million in funds worked on directly and assist in team goal of $20M+, with these goals to increase year over year.

Required

What It Takes to be Successful

Expert working knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations concepts, principles, procedures, and techniques.
Expert knowledge of applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies, etc.
Expert written and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the organization and with outside constituencies. Expert skills in making persuasive and compelling presentations of goals and objectives for a location in order to secure gifts.
Expert organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills. Expert project / program management skills, including skills in setting and meeting program / project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.
Expert level skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Extensive experience in the completion of complex and detailed proposals and related materials.
Extensive experience in working independently with both school and institutional goals in mind.
Highly organized and able to handle multiple projects.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Salesforce or a comparable donor/prospect database system.
Extensive demonstrable experience in stewardship plans leading to additional investments.
Clarity of focus while juggling complex projects and/or deadlines. Ability to meet demanding work schedule expectations
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Seven to ten years' successful professional development and/or fundraising-related experience, preferably in higher education at a R01 university, OR, any equivalent combinations of education and/or experience from which comparable knowledge, skill and abilities have been achieved.

Preferred

Demonstrated ability to read academic and scientific text and convey this information effectively to different audiences. Comfort in speaking effectively in front of large audiences.
Expert knowledge of all aspects of the location, including current issues of concern for both the campus and / or throughout higher education / healthcare, generally. Expert knowledge of the location, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure.
Advanced degree preferred
CFRE certification

Special Conditions

May work long hours to meet fundraising commitments
Local, regional, and national travel
Must maintain a hybrid presence on campus, with a minimum of two days per week on campus and more as needed.

jobs.description:
Experience Senior Living is thrilled to announce The Reserve Sarasota
, scheduled to open in May 2028.
As development progresses, we are beginning the search for an Executive Director
who will play a critical role in pre-operations, sales, and team building during the final stages of development and through opening. This is a unique opportunity to help launch a new community and shape the resident and associate experience from the ground up.

Pre-Operations Responsibilities:

Provide executive leadership during the pre-opening phase, partnering with development, construction, marketing, and corporate teams to ensure operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and a successful community launch.
Lead and support pre-opening sales and marketing efforts, including relationship building in the local market, referral network development, and achievement of initial occupancy goals.
Recruit, onboard, and develop the foundational leadership team, establishing culture, service standards, and operational systems prior to opening.
Oversee pre-opening budgets, policies, and procedures, ensuring alignment with brand standards and a smooth transition from development to full operations

Operating Responsibilities:

Responsible for leading day-to-day operations, including full P & L responsibility.
Ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations, as well as Experience Senior Living's company policies and procedures, standards, and guidelines.
Focuses on creating a safe environment for residents, families, and team members.
Ensure adherence to the Resident's Rights
Focused on resident, family, and team members satisfaction
Be able to analyze data, root causes and develop a plan of action if necessary.
Develop and implement successful strategies regarding labor, occupancy growth, revenue growth, expense control, and quality of services.
Lead morning stand up meetings and ensure minutes are taken for those who were not present.
Strong communications skills; listening, oral and written.
Lead and support all sales and operational strategies, educating all team members of the importance to be part of the sales process.
Actively partnering with the Director of Sales to conduct a quarterly SWOT, and have ongoing weekly, or at times daily discussions, on sales/marketing strategies and help support all sales efforts, including conducting tours, assisting with creative follow ups, outreach, home visits, and building positive relationships with referral partners.

Ensuring that residents have been assessed at the proper level of care. Ensuring that the team members are focused on supporting their independence and current abilities and only assisting in areas of true need. Being available to meet with residents, families and team members regarding any care concerns that need to be addressed.
Coordinating with the Director of Memory Care to address any challenging situations, find creative solutions, assist, and support all dementia training for new team members and ongoing training for existing team members.
Coordinate with the Director of Life Enrichment to ensure the activity calendar is robust, with a wide variety, touching on the whole person, and activities are taking place 7 days per week, including evenings.
Coordinating with the Director of Culinary to ensure menu planning has a wide variety to choose from, alternate choices are available for the residents, and assist in tasting food from meals on a regular basis.
Coordinate with the Director of Maintenance to have ongoing discussions regarding the building, areas of concern, preventative maintenance schedules, room turns completed in a timely manner, required drills being completed, and assist in any coordination for CapEx projects.

Ensure that employee performance reviews are being completed and administered in a timely manner.
Assist in recruiting, hiring, orienting, training, supervising, and evaluating of team members.

Building high-performing teams, keeping morale high and supporting the company culture on a consistent basis.

Also ensuring that each person assigned to be the Manager on Duty has received the proper training and has a solid understanding of the responsibilities while in this role.

May drive company van, bus, or other vehicles from community to social and other destinations.

Being willing to understand, implement and maintain a hospitality environment for residents, families, and team members.

Possess solid performance management and leadership skills, including the ability to communicate performance expectations, coach and document performance strengths and challenges, provide direction and guidance, listen, have on-going conversations regarding performance, including implementing the company's disciplinary process if necessary, completing performance reviews in a timely manner, as well as ensuring all department performance reviews are completed in a timely manner, and providing the necessary support and feedback to all team members.

Knowing when to handle the situation independently or include the necessary individuals to resolve the problem.

Able to clearly present information through the spoken word. Can accurately communicate, providing the necessary level of detail even under stressful or demanding conditions.
Able to relate to routine operations in a manner that is consistent with existing solutions to problems. Conform to and communicate established policies and procedures.

Able to be innovative to create and generate solutions and programs.

Able to research and identify various possibilities to aid in reaching decisions necessary to meet goals.
Identifies, obtains, and effectively allocates the resources required to achieve applicable goals
Build and maintain productive, work-focused relationships with team members, residents, families, referral partners, the executive team, as well as within the community.
Able to work with people in such a manner to support the company's culture, build high-morale teams, work in a team setting to accomplish goals and get results.
Function as a role model for team members by being punctual, neat, clean, and professional in appearance.
Ability to work varied schedules to include weekends, evenings, overnights, and holidays

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer, Jackson North Medical Center
jobs.description:
Summary

Jackson Health System (JHS) continues to expand its reach and strengthen its capacity to deliver world-class care for the vibrant and expanding communities of Miami-Dade. To support this momentum, JHS seeks an innovative, strategic, and mission-driven healthcare executive to serve as the next Chief Operating Officer, Jackson North Medical Center
. This role reflects a strategic investment in our future and recognizes the advancement of leaders whose expanded responsibilities have created this opportunity.

Jackson North Medical Center is a 382-bed, full-service acute care hospital delivering comprehensive medical and surgical care, supported by a high-volume emergency department managing over 60,000 ED visits annually. The campus features 24/7 adult and pediatric emergency care, advanced cardiac care, orthopedics, urology, maternity and women's health, bariatrics, stroke care, neurosciences, and robust rehabilitation programs. Serving tens of thousands of patients each year, Jackson North is a vital access point for high-quality care in North Miami-Dade and a key extension of Jackson Health System's academic and specialty services, ensuring seamless, world-class care close to home.

Leadership Scope

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the operational executive for Jackson North Medical Center, reporting to the CEO and holding a core seat on the hospital's executive leadership team. This position delivers strategic oversight, financial stewardship, and operational leadership across our 382-bed acute care campus and 60,000+ annual emergency department visits. Expanding past traditional operational boundaries, this executive manages high-acuity clinical areas, diagnostic centers, and service lines to ensure seamless care delivery across the hospital.

Key Responsibilities Include

High-Acuity Operations & Patient Flow: Executive oversight of daily hospital operations, patient flow, and high-acuity clinical and procedural departments, including Surgical Services (OR), Interventional Radiology (IR) / Cath Lab, Gastroenterology (GI), Diagnostic Imaging, and Laboratory Services.
Service Line Integration: Local execution, management, and integration of health-system clinical service lines and strategic initiatives across the Jackson North campus.
Quality, Safety & Compliance: Driving continuous quality improvement, patient safety, patient experience, and regulatory compliance across all departments (Joint Commission, CMS, Leapfrog).
Financial Stewardship: Direct management of financial performance, operational budgets, labor productivity, variance analyses, and capital improvement projects.
Capital Strategic Portfolio: Leads a significant capital strategic planning portfolio focused on clinical space renovations and modernization initiatives. Offers the opportunity to define capital priorities and partner with executive and clinical leadership to drive projects that enhance patient care, operational efficiency, clinical growth, and the overall patient experience.
Operational Leadership & Risk: Leadership in operational problem-solving, risk management, emergency preparedness, and facility development.
Culture & Talent Development: Fostering workforce competency, talent development, succession planning, and cultivating a high-performance culture grounded in accountability and collaboration.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a mission-driven, forward-thinking operational executive with:

A master's degree strongly preferred
10+ years of senior operational leadership experience in complex, safety-net, or academic health systems
A proven track record of optimizing hospital operations, patient flow, and clinical support services
Strong strategic, operational, and financial acumen
Demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Commitment to serving diverse and underserved communities

jobs.title: Community Development Director
jobs.description:
Community & Economic Development Director, Tipton County

Tipton County is seeking a highly motivated professional to lead and support community and
economic development initiatives that advance the County’s long-term goals. This position will focus
on business attraction and development, capital investment, strategic planning, workforce and
education initiatives, public-private partnerships, administrative coordination, and special projects.

The position will work closely with the Tipton County Board of Commissioners, County Council,
County departments, community organizations, businesses, educational institutions, economic
development partners, and other public and private stakeholders.

The successful candidate will be a self-directed professional capable of managing multiple priorities,
developing relationships, coordinating complex initiatives, and advancing projects from concept
through implementation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Economic and Community Development

● Promote Tipton County as a location for business investment, expansion, and development.
Identify, pursue, and assist with new business and economic development opportunities.
● Support efforts to attract and increase private capital investment within Tipton County.
● Build and maintain relationships with existing businesses and assist with business retention and
expansion initiatives.
● Coordinate with local, regional, and state economic development organizations and other
strategic partners.
● Develop and maintain relationships with developers, site selectors, businesses, utilities,
educational institutions, and other organizations involved in economic and community
development.
● Assist with the development and implementation of short- and long-term economic development

Jackson Health System (JHS) continues to expand its reach and strengthen its capacity to deliver world-class care for the vibrant and expanding communities of Miami-Dade. Jackson North Medical Center is a 382-bed, full-service acute care hospital delivering comprehensive medical and surgical care, supported by a high-volume emergency department managing over 60,000 ED visits annually. The campus features 24/7 adult and pediatric emergency care, advanced cardiac care, orthopedics, urology, maternity and women's health, bariatrics, stroke care, neurosciences, and robust rehabilitation programs. Serving tens of thousands of patients each year, Jackson North is a vital access point for high-quality care in North Miami-Dade and a key extension of Jackson Health System's academic and specialty services, ensuring seamless, world-class care close to home.

Leadership Scope

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the operational executive for Jackson North Medical Center, reporting to the CEO and holding a core seat on the hospital's executive leadership team. This position delivers strategic oversight, financial stewardship, and operational leadership across our 382-bed acute care campus and 60,000+ annual emergency department visits. Expanding past traditional operational boundaries, this executive manages high-acuity clinical areas, diagnostic centers, and service lines to ensure seamless care delivery across the hospital.

High-Acuity Operations & Patient Flow: Executive oversight of daily hospital operations, patient flow, and high-acuity clinical and procedural departments, including Surgical Services (OR), Interventional Radiology (IR) / Cath Lab, Gastroenterology (GI), Diagnostic Imaging, and Laboratory Services.
Service Line Integration: Local execution, management, and integration of health-system clinical service lines and strategic initiatives across the Jackson North campus.
Quality, Safety & Compliance: Driving continuous quality improvement, patient safety, patient experience, and regulatory compliance across all departments (Joint Commission, CMS, Leapfrog).

Offers the opportunity to define capital priorities and partner with executive and clinical leadership to drive projects that enhance patient care, operational efficiency, clinical growth, and the overall patient experience.
Operational Leadership & Risk: Leadership in operational problem-solving, risk management, emergency preparedness, and facility development.
Culture & Talent Development: Fostering workforce competency, talent development, succession planning, and cultivating a high-performance culture grounded in accountability and collaboration.

A master's degree strongly preferred
